title: Viruses and Antivirus
part: Part D — Networks and the Internet

blocks.html: After studying this chapter you will be able to:

items.html: define malware and computer virus and trace a short history of viruses
describe the phases of a virus and how viruses spread
classify viruses and other malware such as worms, trojans, spyware, ransomware and rootkits
recognise the symptoms of an infected computer
explain how antivirus software works and use it correctly
follow good practices to prevent infection and recover from it

blocks.html: Malware (malicious software) is any software written to harm a computer, steal data or misuse a system without the owner's permission.

Definition: A computer virus is a type of malware that attaches itself to a program or file and replicates (copies itself) when that file is run, spreading to other files and computers, and usually causing damage.
Just as a biological virus needs a living cell, a computer virus needs a host file and a user action (opening the file) to spread.

rows: Creeper, an experimental self-copying program on ARPANET, displays "I'm the creeper, catch me if you can!"; Reaper was written to remove it — the first "antivirus"
Elk Cloner spreads through floppy disks on Apple II computers
Brain, the first virus for IBM PCs, infects the boot sector of floppy disks
Melissa and ILOVEYOU spread by email across the world
WannaCry ransomware locks hundreds of thousands of computers in over 150 countries, including systems in India

items.html: Dormant phase — the virus is present but inactive, hidden in a host file.
Propagation phase — it copies itself into other files, disks or across a network.
Triggering phase — a condition activates it: a date, a number of runs, or a user action.
Execution phase — the payload runs: showing messages, deleting or corrupting files, slowing the system or stealing data.

blocks.html: Virus vs worm vs trojan: a virus needs a host file and a user to run it; a worm spreads on its own; a trojan does not copy itself but tricks the user into installing it.
Antivirus software is a utility that prevents, detects and removes malware.

items.html: Signature-based detection — compares files with a database of known malware "fingerprints" (signatures). This database must be updated regularly.
Heuristic and behaviour-based detection — looks for suspicious behaviour (e.g. a program trying to encrypt many files quickly), to catch new, unknown malware.
Real-time protection — scans files as they are opened, downloaded or copied.
Quarantine — moves suspected files to a safe, locked area where they cannot run; you can then delete or restore them.
Cloud protection — checks new files against the company's online database.
Web and email protection — blocks dangerous websites and attachments.

rows: Checks the places malware usually hides; takes a few minutes
Checks every file on all drives; takes longer
Checks a chosen drive, folder or pen drive
Runs before Windows starts, to remove stubborn malware

blocks.html: Windows Security (Microsoft Defender) is built into Windows. Other well-known products include Quick Heal and K7 Security (both Indian companies), Norton, McAfee, Kaspersky, Bitdefender, Avast and AVG. Phones also have built-in protection, such as Google Play Protect on Android.
Use only one real-time antivirus at a time — two can conflict and slow the computer.

A firewall checks network traffic coming in and going out and blocks connections that are not allowed. Antivirus deals with harmful files; the firewall deals with harmful connections. Keep both turned on.

items.html: Keep the operating system, browser and apps updated.
Keep antivirus turned on and updated; run a full scan regularly.
Scan pen drives before opening them; turn off AutoPlay.
Download software only from official sources; never use pirated or cracked software.
Do not open unexpected attachments or links, even from friends.
Do not enable macros in documents from unknown sources.
Use a standard user account for daily work rather than an administrator account.
Take regular backups on an external drive or cloud, kept disconnected.
Ignore pop-ups that claim your computer is infected.
Disconnect from the internet and network to stop the spread.
Run a full scan and an offline/boot-time scan; quarantine or delete what is found.
Change important passwords from a different, clean device.
Restore damaged files from backup.
If ransomware strikes, do not pay — report it on cybercrime.gov.in and seek expert
In severe cases, reinstall the operating system.

blocks.html: India's CERT-In runs the Cyber Swachhta Kendra (Botnet Cleaning and Malware Analysis Centre), which provides free tools and advice to clean infected systems.
Did you know? The word "virus" for self-copying programs was popularised by the researcher Fred Cohen in 1983, who studied how such programs spread.
Aim: To use antivirus and security tools correctly.

items.html: Check protection status. Open Windows Security (Start → type Windows Security). Note whether Virus & threat protection, Firewall and App & browser control are on.
Update definitions. Click Protection updates → Check for updates and note the date of the latest definitions.
Quick scan. Run a Quick scan and record the time taken and the result.
Custom scan of a pen drive. Right-click a pen drive → Scan with Microsoft Defender.
Quarantine. Open Protection history and see whether any item was quarantined or removed.
AutoPlay off. In Settings → Bluetooth & devices → AutoPlay, turn AutoPlay off.
Spot the fake. Your teacher will show screenshots of real and fake virus warnings. Identify the fakes and explain the clues.
Malware is any harmful software; a virus attaches to a host file and replicates when the file runs.
Virus history: Creeper (1971), Elk Cloner (1982), Brain (1986), ILOVEYOU (2000), WannaCry (2017).
A virus passes through dormant, propagation, triggering and execution phases; it spreads through pen drives, attachments, downloads, websites and networks.
Types of viruses: boot sector, file infector, macro, resident, polymorphic, multipartite and stealth.
Other malware: worm, trojan, spyware, keylogger, adware, ransomware, rootkit, botnet malware and scareware.
Antivirus uses signatures, heuristics, real-time scanning and quarantine; scans can be quick, full, custom or boot-time.
Prevent infection with updates, antivirus, safe downloads, backups and caution; if infected, disconnect, scan, change passwords and restore from backup.
